name: Accordion
purpose: A disclosure control that collapses/expands a section of content behind a titled header. Used to reduce clutter and cognitive load on content-heavy pages or where a range of user needs must be covered (e.g. FAQs). For a single disclosure on its own, prefer an Expand link rather than a lone accordion.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: Default accordion on white surfaces; titled section disclosure. Title uses the font-4 scale (covers display scales 1-3) or font-5.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Compact, link-style disclosure for dense layouts or within running content; smaller footprint (size 5/6).

accessibility.role: Header is a button that controls a collapsible region (disclosure pattern)
accessibility.keyboard: Header is reachable in tab order; Enter and Space toggle open/closed
accessibility.focus: REVIEW: the Figma component set defines default/hover/pressed but no explicit focus-visible state — confirm a visible focus indicator exists in code
accessibility.screenReader: Header button exposes aria-expanded reflecting open state; arrow icon is decorative (aria-hidden); content region associated to the header (aria-controls / region labelled by the title)

antiPatterns: Using a single accordion on its own — use an Expand link instead (per HSBC guidance)
Changing an accordion title after the user completes its action (e.g. relabelling to 'Personal details entered') — titles must stay stable (per HSBC guidance)
Title case or inconsistent casing — titles are written in sentence case (per HSBC guidance)
Vague or overlong titles — keep concise, descriptive, and consistent in grammar and tone (per HSBC guidance)
REVIEW (inferred): hiding required or critical information inside a collapsed panel
REVIEW (inferred): deeply nesting accordions within accordions
REVIEW (inferred): hard-coding the header text colour or rule colour instead of binding text/default and border/subtle tokens

tokenValidation.against: token store re-based on Figma native variable export (semantic-colour.json, spacing.json, typography.json)
tokenValidation.result: PASS — all 9 token refs resolve; none deprecated
tokenValidation.notes: Colour tokens resolve in both light and dark modes. background-pressed = tertiary/background/pressed (light #767676) is intentionally strong: per Dave, WCAG state differentiation needs more than a single colour change, and active/pressed warrants more contrast than hover — the pressed state combines two colour changes plus an icon change, which clears that bar. Acknowledged as possibly heavy-handed; may be revisited but not a defect. dark-mode semantics are partly in the in-progress Sutherland remap; re-check if those modes change.
